title: How to reorder slides in Keynote on Mac: drag, outline and Light Table steps
metaTitle: How to reorder slides in Keynote on Mac: 3 ways
description: Learn how to reorder slides in Keynote on Mac by dragging in the navigator, Outline or Light Table, with multi-select and undo tips.
targetKeyword: how to reorder slides in keynote on mac
secondaryKeywords: move slides in Keynote on Mac
intro: To reorder slides in Keynote on Mac, click a slide in the navigator and drag it up or down to its new spot. Apple documents dragging as the method, and it does not list a menu command for the job.
tldr: Click a slide in the navigator, then drag it up or down to its new position.
Select several slides with Command-click, then drag the group together.
Use the View menu button in the toolbar to switch to Outline or Light Table if the drag fails.
Press Command-Z to undo a move you did not mean to make.

blocks.text: Drag a slide in the navigator

The navigator is the column of slide thumbnails on the left side of the Keynote window. It is the default view on Mac, so it is the first place to look. Apple's reorder page describes dragging as the way to move slides, and it does not list a menu command for the job.

To move one slide, click its thumbnail once so it is selected. Press and hold the thumbnail, drag it up or down, and let go at the spot you want. That is the whole method. The same drag works for the first slide and the last one.
On a long deck, drag slowly. A fast flick can carry a slide past the spot you wanted, and then you have to drag it back. Check the order from the first slide to the last before you save.
Move several slides at once

Sometimes you need to move a section, not a single slide. Select the group first, then drag the group as one unit. Apple's reorder page says to click the first slide and then Command-click each other slide you want to move.

Apple's keyboard shortcuts page adds a second method. Shift-drag or Shift-click selects a range, and Command-click adds or removes one slide that is not next to the others. The two pages do not fully agree, so test both on your version before you rely on either one.

Here is a worked example. Say slides 4, 5 and 9 belong after slide 12. Click slide 4, Command-click slides 5 and 9, then drag the three together to the spot below slide 12. Check the result, and press Command-Z if the group lands in the wrong place.

items: Command-click adds or removes one slide that is not next to the others.
Shift-click extends the selection through a range of slides.
Shift-drag selects a range while you drag across the thumbnails.
Delete removes every selected slide, so check the selection before you press it.
Command-D duplicates the selected slides when you want a copy first.

blocks.text: Group slides under a parent slide
Keynote can nest slides in the navigator. Drag a slide to the right and it indents under the slide above it, which groups the two. Use this to hang detail slides under a section slide.
The keyboard does the same job. Tab indents the selected slides, and Shift-Tab moves indented slides back to the left. Use Tab when you want to group a batch of slides in one go.

blocks.title: Easy to group by accident
blocks.text: A quick drag to the right can indent a slide you meant to move up or down. If the slide suddenly sits under the one above it, press Shift-Tab or Command-Z.
Reorder slides in Outline view

Outline view shows your slide titles and text as a list. It helps when you write the deck first and shape the order later. To switch, click the View menu button in the toolbar and choose Outline. Apple's view page names the button that way, so look for it in the toolbar.

Drag the bullet to move a line. Apple says to drag the bullet itself, not its text. You can also drag a slide icon to change slide order. Outline view is a good place to catch a weak slide title, because you read the whole argument at once.

blocks.title: Outline text size
blocks.text: The font size in Outline view is set in Keynote > Settings > General. Change it there if the list is hard to read on your screen.
Reorder slides in Light Table

Light Table shows many slides at once as a grid of thumbnails. Switch with the View menu button in the toolbar, then choose Light Table. This view suits a long deck, because you can see the flow without scrolling a narrow column.

Use the thumbnail-size slider in the bottom-right corner to make thumbnails bigger or smaller. Smaller thumbnails show more of the deck at once. Larger ones make it easier to spot small text problems before you move anything.

Light Table also has a Hide skipped slides checkbox. Turn it on to hide slides you have skipped, so the run of the deck is easier to follow. You can skip or unskip the selected slide with Shift-Command-H.
Command-Up and Command-Down select the first or last slide. Add Shift to extend the selection to the first or last slide. That is faster than dragging a long way across a big grid.

blocks.text: Which Keynote version you need

Apple's What's New page lists Keynote 15.4 as the newest version for Mac. It requires macOS 26 or later. The page does not mention changes to the navigator or to reordering, so the steps above come from Apple's reorder and view pages.

Keynote 15.1 came out on January 28, 2026, as a separate app instead of an update to the old one, according to Wikipedia. TidBITS says 15.1 requires macOS 15.6 or later and installs next to the 14.5 version. It does not show in the App Store Updates list, so search for it.

If you run an older Keynote, check the menus on your own screen. The drag method is the same in the views Apple documents. Apple's reorder page does not give a version, so confirm the details on your copy.
Reorder slides in Keynote for iCloud in a browser

Keynote for iCloud works in a browser. Apple documents one reorder method there: drag a slide, or the top slide of a closed group, up or down in the slide navigator. When the target is past the window edge, the list scrolls as you drag.
Apple's iCloud page does not document Command-click, Shift-click, or menu options for reordering in the browser. Do not assume the Mac shortcuts work there. Test on a small deck first.

Browser support comes from Apple's general iCloud requirements page, not from a Keynote page. On Mac it lists Safari 13.1 or later, Firefox 128 or later, Google Chrome 130 or later, and Microsoft Edge 130 or later.
When a slide will not move

The most common problem is a drag that never starts. The thumbnail gets selected, but nothing moves. Start by dragging more slowly, and make sure you press on the thumbnail itself, not on the empty space beside the list.

An old Apple Community answer says a blue line with an arrow shows that a drag is registering. That thread is from the Mac OS X 10.7.5 era, so the detail may not match current versions. It suggests View > Light Table, which current Keynote labels as the View menu button.
If the drag still fails, switch to Light Table and drag there. The grid view often works when the navigator does not, and it costs you nothing to try.
Keyboard shortcuts for moving slides
Apple's shortcuts page lists the keys that matter for this task. The list below covers only the keys that affect order, selection, and undo, so you do not have to hunt through the full page.

items: Shift-Command-H skips or unskips the selected slide.
Tab and Shift-Tab indent and outdent slides in the navigator.
Command-Up and Command-Down select the first or last slide in Light Table.

blocks.text: Some shortcuts can be changed in System Settings, so a key may do something else on your Mac. Apple's shortcuts page says so. If a key does nothing, check your keyboard shortcut settings before you assume the feature is missing.
Mistakes people make when reordering slides

items: Dragging the words in Outline view instead of the bullet. Drag the bullet, as Apple says.
Assuming Command-click selects a range. Shift-click is the range key on Apple's shortcuts page.
Pressing Delete with a stray selection. Delete removes every selected slide.
Dragging right by accident and grouping a slide under the wrong parent.
Expecting Mac shortcuts to work in Keynote for iCloud. Apple documents only the drag there.

blocks.text: Each of these is easy to undo. Command-Z works best right after the move, so press it before you make another change. Undo one step at a time until the order looks right.
Next steps after you reorder

Once the order is right, check the flow from start to finish. Look at each section's first slide, because that is where a wrong order is easiest to spot. A transition that looked fine before the move may feel odd after it.

Your next job is usually the detail work. Add motion with the steps in [How to add a transition in Keynote on Mac](/how-to/add-a-transition-in-keynote). If you present from a laptop with a projector, read [How to play a slideshow on a second display in Keynote on Mac](/how-to/play-a-slideshow-on-a-second-display-in-keynote).

If you use one layout across the deck, [How to edit the master slide in Keynote on Mac](/how-to/edit-the-master-slide-in-keynote) covers the layouts that new slides start from. Those layouts decide how each slide looks after a move.

faq.question: Is there a menu command to reorder slides in Keynote on Mac?
faq.answer: Not that Apple documents. Apple's reorder page describes dragging a slide in the navigator, the presentation outline, or Light Table. Use one of those views instead of looking for a menu item.

faq.question: Why won't my slide move when I drag it?
faq.answer: Drag more slowly and make sure you press on the thumbnail. If nothing moves, switch to Light Table from the View menu button and drag there. An old Apple Community answer names a blue line with an arrow as a sign the drag is registering, but that thread is from the Mac OS X 10.7.5 era.

faq.question: Which key selects a range of slides in Keynote?
faq.answer: Apple's keyboard shortcuts page says Shift-click extends the selection and Shift-drag selects a range. Apple's reorder page only mentions Command-click for adding slides. Test both on your version.

faq.question: What is the difference between skipping and deleting a slide?
faq.answer: Shift-Command-H skips or unskips a slide, and pressing it again reverses the change. Delete removes every selected slide. If you delete by mistake, press Command-Z right away.

faq.question: Can I reorder slides in Keynote for iCloud?
faq.answer: Yes, by dragging a slide up or down in the slide navigator in a supported browser. Apple's iCloud page does not document Command-click, Shift-click, or menu options for reordering there.

faq.question: Which Keynote version do I need for these steps?
faq.answer: This page is written against Keynote 15.4, which requires macOS 26 or later, according to Apple's What's New page. Keynote 15.1 requires macOS 15.6 or later, according to TidBITS. Check your version in the app before you follow the steps.

faq.question: Does Light Table make reordering a long deck faster?
faq.answer: It can. You see many slides at once, and the thumbnail slider lets you shrink or grow the grid. Shift-Command-Up and Shift-Command-Down extend a selection to the first or last slide.

steps.name: Open the deck and show the navigator
steps.text: Open the presentation in Keynote on Mac. The navigator is the default view, so the slide thumbnails should sit in a column on the left. If you do not see them, click the View menu button in the toolbar and choose Navigator.
steps.tip: The navigator is where you will do most of the reordering, so keep it open.

steps.name: Select the slide you want to move
steps.text: Click the thumbnail once. The slide is selected, and the rest of the deck stays where it is.
steps.tip: If you want to move a whole section, use the multi-select step next.

steps.name: Drag it to the new position
steps.text: Press and hold on the selected thumbnail. Drag it up or down, then let go where you want the slide to land. Drag slowly on a long deck so the drop lands where you meant.

steps.name: Select several slides
steps.text: Click the first slide, then Command-click each other slide you want to move. Apple's reorder page gives this method.
steps.tip: Command-click a selected slide again to remove it from the selection.

steps.name: Select a range with Shift
steps.text: Click the first slide in the range, then Shift-click the last one. Everything between them is selected. Apple's shortcuts page gives this method, and it differs from the reorder page, so test it.
steps.tip: Try the method on two slides before you move a long range.

steps.name: Group slides under a parent
steps.text: Select the slides you want to nest, then press Tab to indent them under the slide above. Press Shift-Tab to move them back to the left. You can also drag a slide to the right to indent it.
steps.tip: Indenting groups slides under the one above, so check the parent slide before you go on.

steps.name: Switch to Outline view
steps.text: Click the View menu button in the toolbar and choose Outline. Drag the bullet beside a slide title to move that slide. You can also drag a slide icon to change the order.
steps.tip: Drag the bullet, not its text. Apple's view page says so.

steps.name: Make the outline text easier to read
steps.text: If the Outline list is hard to read, open Keynote > Settings > General and change the Outline View Font. The setting controls the font size in Outline view.

steps.name: Switch to Light Table for a grid view
steps.text: Click the View menu button in the toolbar and choose Light Table. Drag a thumbnail to a new spot in the grid. Use the slider in the bottom-right corner to resize thumbnails. Press Shift-Command-Up or Shift-Command-Down to extend a selection to the first or last slide.
steps.tip: Turn on Hide skipped slides if skipped slides get in the way of the flow.

steps.name: Undo a move you did not want
steps.text: Press Command-Z to undo the last move. Press it again to step back further, one change at a time.
steps.tip: Undo also reverses an accidental Tab that grouped slides.

troubleshooting.problem: The slide won't move when I drag it
troubleshooting.fix: Drag more slowly and press on the thumbnail itself. If nothing moves, switch to Light Table from the View menu button in the toolbar and drag there.

troubleshooting.problem: Shift-click and Command-click select different slides than the pages describe
troubleshooting.fix: Apple's reorder page and shortcuts page disagree on multi-select. Test Shift-click for ranges and Command-click for single slides on your version. Select one slide at a time if both fail.

troubleshooting.problem: A slide ended up indented under another slide
troubleshooting.fix: Press Shift-Tab to move the slide back to the left, or press Command-Z to undo the grouping.

troubleshooting.problem: I pressed Delete and lost slides
troubleshooting.fix: Press Command-Z right away, before you do anything else. If you already saved, reopen your last copy of the deck.

troubleshooting.problem: Command-click does nothing in Keynote for iCloud
troubleshooting.fix: Apple documents only the drag in the browser. Move one slide at a time there, or open the deck in Keynote on Mac for bulk moves.

troubleshooting.problem: A keyboard shortcut does nothing on my Mac
troubleshooting.fix: Apple says some shortcuts can be changed in System Settings. Check your keyboard shortcut settings, or use the drag method instead.
